llm_findings: The authoritative Block.forward confirms the mechanism: q_in/k_in/v_in and the Q/K shift are computed before x = x + self.local_conv(norm(x)); serial attention subsequently reads the pre-convolution snapshots. USE_LOCAL_CONV and TRAIN_LOCAL_CONV are True, and setup_optimizer registers the convolution weights.

The plan isolates one causal factor: move the existing convolution residual update ahead of snapshot construction on the default serial path. Toggle plumbing and checkpoint persistence support that change; kernels, parameters, optimizer, precision, and alternative block paths remain unchanged. Pre-smoke work is limited to train.py edits and deterministic syntax/diff/static review.

CURRENT_STATE.md's 2026-09-23 primary-source override explicitly identifies this ordering repair as an untested lead. DECISION_LOG.md's discarded --nki-local-conv experiment changed kernel implementation, not convolution-to-attention wiring, so it does not close this direction.

The change is competition-legal under README.md: it modifies model architecture using existing trained components, without pretrained weights, external data, or evaluator changes. CausalConv left-pads by kernel_size minus one, and downstream attention remains causal. The plan explicitly requires saved-toggle restoration and False for legacy checkpoints lacking the key; the exact patch must implement that fallback rather than merely inherit the new import-time default.

The predicted -0.002 public BPB delta and step count within 2% are falsifiable against the controller's matched seed-42 full-chip control, recorded at 1.005734 BPB / 2071 steps on trn21. Unchanged operation count does not guarantee unchanged throughput because dependencies and compiler scheduling change; the smoke throughput gate and full-run comparability rule appropriately test this risk. Runtime causality and checkpoint-evaluation checks are smoke conditions, not implementation prerequisites.
